# Independent audit: primitive rays and the quadratic sequence bound

Audited files:

- `candidate 6de52361fe012092`
- `candidate efcef1959b4a9d5f`

Both proofs pass within their expressly stated scopes. Neither is a proof
of OC. The two clarifications raised during this audit—the absence of
additional integer fibers in the convex hull of the positive fibers,
and the phrase “oppositely oriented weak inequalities”—are already
incorporated in the first file.

## 1. Primitive rays

The mixed-integer translation is legitimate because the actual measure
centroid has integer base. Its continuous coordinate is the actual
first moment divided by total mass, not an average of unweighted fiber
centroids. The positive mass weights give both displayed zero-moment
equations after translation.

The origin belongs to the relative interior of the convex hull of the
positive fibers. More explicitly, the positive weighted base average
puts zero in the relative interior of the base hull. Each positive fiber
has all continuous directions in its affine span; hence the affine span
of the new body is exactly `V x R^d`. A supporting functional with zero
measure integral must vanish on each positive fiber: its restriction is
continuous and nonnegative, and every such fiber is full dimensional.
It therefore vanishes on the full relative affine span. This rules out
a proper supporting hyperplane through zero.

There is also no overlooked zero-volume integer index in the new body.
Every point of `conv(P)` is a convex combination of positive-fiber
indices. The corresponding Minkowski combination of full-dimensional
fiber bodies is full dimensional. At an integer base, this combination
is contained in the original fiber, so that index was already in `P`.
In particular the gauge floor cannot count an extra zero-volume index
beyond the last listed positive fiber on a ray.

For `k>0`, the substitution `x=k s` has Jacobian `k^d`. Multiplication
by either the base index `k p` or the continuous coordinate `k s` adds
one power of `k`. Thus `f_p` has the correct mass weight `k^d`, whereas
both first moments require `g_p` with weight `k^(d+1)`. The no-gap and
nesting assertions follow from convex combinations with the actual
origin and do not require that every source fiber contain its own
continuous origin.

The gauge is finite and positive away from zero in its relative ambient
space. Since `p` is nonzero, `(p,s)` is never the zero vector. Positive
homogeneity and closed membership give exactly

    k(p,s) belongs to C_* iff k rho(p,s)<=1.

Consequently the floor convention includes every equality radius,
including positive-volume plateaus caused by a vertical facet. The
closed-cap identity similarly retains the entire central fiber when
`u=0` and any complete ray with `a dot p=0`. A nonzero ambient normal
whose restriction to the relative affine span vanishes also gives the
correct identity: the whole measure lies on the boundary.

In the one-integer-coordinate specialization, the reflected negative
ray has coordinates `(-k,-k s)`. Its Jacobian in absolute value remains
`k^d`; its continuous first moment changes sign; and its cap condition
becomes the weak inequality `a+u dot s<=0`. Both ray inequalities are
closed. Empty ray families and the case where the only positive base is
zero are harmless. No extension to intrinsic dimension below `d` is
used or asserted.

## 2. The exact one-arm minimum

For `h=0` the claimed value is `1/3`. For `h>=1`, the decomposition of
the concave error sequence into its endpoint affine function and the
discrete tents is exact. The tent coefficients are the negative second
differences and are nonnegative. Direct summation gives

    sum G_t=t(h-t)/2,
    sum i G_t=t(h-t)(h+t)/6,
    sum r_i i=0,
    sum r_i G_t=t(h-t)(h+1-t)/(3(2h+1))>0.

Therefore the linear cross term in the quadratic difference is
nonnegative, and the sum of error squares establishes both the minimum
and uniqueness. This proof permits arbitrary real concave sequences on
the arm and needs no compactness assumption. As an independent check,
the proposed minimizer satisfies

    sum v_i=(h+1)^2/(2h+1),
    sum v_i^2=(h+1)(2h+3)/(3(2h+1)).

Their difference with coefficient `2/3` is exactly the stated minimum.

Reversing the left arm preserves concavity. Subtracting the duplicate
peak term gives exactly

    Q-(2/3)mM >= (m^2/6)
        [1/(2j+1)+1/(2(N-1-j)+1)].

The two minimizing affine arms join with decreasing slopes, remain
positive, and attain the claimed bound. Endpoint peaks and `N=1` are
included. For the symmetric triangular sharpness sequence on
`-h,...,h`, direct finite formulas are

    m=1,  M=h,  Q=2h/3+1/(3h),

so the ratio is exactly `2/3+1/(3h^2)` and tends to `2/3`.

## 3. The interval cap consequence

An integer base translation followed by the stated affine continuous
shear and reflection preserves the lattice, interval lengths, cap
masses, and both centroid equations. The transformed lower endpoints
are convex, the upper endpoints concave, and their difference is a
positive concave sequence on the consecutive positive-fiber indices.

Under the express hypothesis that no full positive interval is captured,
all lower endpoints are strictly negative and the actual closed-cap
mass is exactly `A=sum (r_i)_+`. This formula correctly counts a wholly
excluded interval as zero, including an interval with right endpoint
zero. The centroid equation gives `sum w_i r_i=Q/2`, with the negative
terms still present. Discarding only those negative terms gives

    m A >= sum w_i (r_i)_+ >= Q/2.

Thus `A/M>1/3` follows with no loss from excluded fibers. The argument
explicitly does not cover vertical halfspaces or caps containing a
whole positive interval; no such case is silently included in its
conclusion.

No mathematical defect or untracked constant remains in either file.
